verdict: PARTIAL. Everything that can be checked without more GPU memory passed: byte-verified download, header/config/registry cross-check, and — importantly — the kernels are proven correct at this model's dimensions. The full model does NOT run on this machine: it allocates, then loses the GPU device on the first inference pass. Registry left at EXPERIMENTAL. The live gate needs a second physical device.

provenance.verification: HF's X-Linked-ETag read before download, local file hashed after. Byte length and SHA-256 both match exactly.

gate1_headerProbe.note: GGUF header, the model's published config.json, and models/registry.mjs agree on every field the engine depends on.

gate2_soloLoad.loadOutcome: SUCCEEDED — all 36 layers plus the tied embedding table were allocated. Notably higher than the ~1.9 GB previously assumed to be this GPU's ceiling.
gate2_soloLoad.loadNote: Slow and hostile to the tab: the fetch/stage phase pinned the main thread hard enough that a trivial `window.x` read timed out at 45 s more than once. Weights are staged into CPU memory in full before upload, so a 4.2 GB model needs 4.2 GB of tab RAM as well as GPU memory.
gate2_soloLoad.inferenceOutcome: FAILED — the GPU device was lost on the first inference pass.

deviceLost.message: A valid external Instance reference no longer exists.

gate2_soloLoad.surfacedAs: GPU device lost (unknown): A valid external Instance reference no longer exists. — this worker cannot continue; it must be re-planned around.
gate2_soloLoad.interpretation: Not the Bug 1 class (no validation error was recorded, and the buffers were not silently zeroed). This is real device loss under memory pressure: the adapter will hand out 4 GB of buffers and the driver then dies trying to actually run over them. Exactly the case acquireDevice()'s own comment warns about -- the adapter's reported limits are not a promise that much memory is free.

gate3_kernelsAreCorrectAtThisScale.why: A full-model failure alone cannot distinguish 'this model is too big for this GPU' from 'this model is broken in our engine at hidden=2560'. This test separates them.
gate3_kernelsAreCorrectAtThisScale.outcome: PASSED — loaded and ran. embedRun() returned a hidden state of length 2560 (correct for this model), every value finite, all 2560 values non-zero, and a second successive call also succeeded.
gate3_kernelsAreCorrectAtThisScale.conclusion: The engine, the Q8_0 dequantization, and the WGSL kernels are correct at 4B's dimensions (hidden 2560, 32 query heads over 8 KV heads). The full-model failure is a capacity ceiling on this specific GPU, not a correctness or shape bug.

measuredCeilingOnThisGpu.practicalCeiling: somewhere at or above 2235 MB and below 4076 MB on this AMD gcn-5 adapter

whyASingleMachineCannotCloseThisPhase: Every 'device' used in this session's split tests is a browser context on ONE physical GPU. Splitting 4B across two or three contexts does not reduce the total GPU memory required -- it is ~4.2 GB either way, which is above the ceiling measured above. So no split arrangement on this machine can run 4B. This is not a limitation of the scheduler or the room; it is arithmetic.

whatWouldCloseIt.requirement: Two genuinely separate physical devices, each with its own GPU.
whatWouldCloseIt.budget: A 2-way even split needs ~2308 MB on the host (it carries the 394 MB tied embedding table) and ~1914 MB on the worker. Both figures sit near the 2235 MB footprint this GPU has already run successfully, so a pair of comparable machines should manage it.
whatWouldCloseIt.note: This is the first rung where the product claim stops being a demonstration and becomes the only way to run the model at all -- which makes it the most valuable rung to show, and the one that most needs real hardware.
whatWouldCloseIt.threeDeviceTarget: The blueprint treats a genuine 3-device test as required for this phase's exit gate, not optional. That needs three physical devices: ~1670 MB host, ~1276 MB per worker.

stillOpenForThisModel: One-device deterministic golden — cannot be produced here; the device dies before any token is generated.
Two-device split equivalence, live room run, and worker-loss recovery — all need a second physical GPU.
External reference cross-check against transformers — deliberately not run. There is no room-side output to compare it against yet, so it would prove nothing about this project.
Three-device capacity demonstration — the blueprint's stated exit gate for this rung.
registryStatus: EXPERIMENTAL. The loader and engine can be tried and the kernels are proven correct at this scale, but there is no recorded end-to-end generation, so it does not meet this project's own definition of Verified.
